subject: Warm-residency econ breakdown + pilot plan
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <treynolds@fincloud.com>, Sara Liu <sara@fincloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-05T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + ask: token volumes & budget window

Thanks for the call today — good conversation. Short recap and a couple of asks so we can model a clean pilot: 

Summary from our side:
- Primary product surface: conversational support flows + proactive suggestions (mostly short prompts, ~250-500 tokens per interaction).
- Expected active users for pilot: 120–200k DAU (you mentioned high reuse across common flows).
- Key success criteria: reduce per-interaction latency <300ms P95, and hit an effective cost target that lets you justify replacing existing rules with LLMs.

Two asks so we can size pricing: 
1) Can you confirm a conservative monthly token projection for the pilot (rough ballpark is fine): prompts vs completions if you can (e.g., 30M prompts / 90M completions = 120M tokens)?
2) Confirm the internal budget window (you said ‘mid tens of thousands / month’ — can you give a $/1M tokens target range you’d be comfortable with for the pilot?)

What I’ll do next: run a back-of-envelope effective $/1M tokens table for three cache-hit scenarios (you said many calls hit the same 10–20 prompt templates, so prefix residency should help). I’ll loop in Marissa and Ben for formal pricing & SOW.

Attachments: none on this note.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake | Senior AE, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0183
From: Tom Reynolds <treynolds@fincloud.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Liu <sara@fincloud.com>, Procurement <procurement@fincloud.com>
Date: 2026-05-06T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + ask: token volumes & budget window

Thanks Jordan — quick answers inline: 

- Token projection (pilot, month 1): approx 120M total tokens (we expect prompt:completion ratio close to 1:2 on average because completions tend to be longer)
  - Prompts ~40M, Completions ~80M -> 120M tokens total
- Working set notes: we see ~18–22 canonical templates that account for ~45% of prompt volume (good candidate for prefix residency).
- Budget window: for an initial pilot we have flexibility; finance has penciled $40k–$90k/month depending on SLA and measurable ROI. At a commercial level, product is targeting an effective spend no higher than $25k per 1M tokens if the quality and latency pan out — but there’s room to trade off based on caching performance.

Looping in Procurement for a heads-up on timelines.

— Tom
Tom Reynolds | Head of Integrations, FinCloud
treynolds@fincloud.com | +1 212-555-0102
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <treynolds@fincloud.com>, Sara Liu <sara@fincloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-06T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + ask: token volumes & budget window

Perfect — thanks Tom. Looping in Marissa and Ben to validate pricing and to propose a short pilot SOW. Per our call here are three back-of-envelope scenarios (assumptions called out):

Assumptions (for quick modeling):
- Baseline raw model compute cost (no cache): $120 per 1M tokens
- Average cache op overhead (extra fast-lookup + KV traffic): $8 per 1M tokens (adds even when a hit occurs)
- Prefix residency re-use only affects compute portion (not the lookup overhead)

Scenarios (effective $/1M tokens):
- Low hit (15%): effective = 120*(1 - 0.15) + 8 = $110 / 1M tokens
- Mid hit (40%): effective = 120*(1 - 0.40) + 8 = $80 / 1M tokens
- High hit (65%): effective = 120*(1 - 0.65) + 8 = $50 / 1M tokens

Applied to Tom’s pilot estimate (120M tokens / month):
- Low hit -> monthly spend ≈ 120 * $110 = $13,200 (per million units scaled -> actually 120M /1M * $110 = $13,200)
- Mid hit -> monthly spend ≈ 120 * $80 = $9,600
- High hit -> monthly spend ≈ 120 * $50 = $6,000

Notes & caveats:
- The above is illustrative and intentionally conservative on cache savings (we left some non-cacheable system overhead in the compute number).
- If the working set is as tight as you suggested (~20 templates = ~45% of prompts), we’d expect mid->high hit during steady-state; cross-session affinity and prefetching can push you toward the high-hit scenario for many flows.
- These numbers exclude enterprise discounts, dedicated capacity pricing, and any committed volume tiers — Marissa will propose those next.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Marissa/Ben: can you confirm whether we can target a commercial effective rate that lands in Tom’s $25k / 1M target for this pilot (Tom, you specifically said $25k target as an upper bound; I want to align expectations on units).
2) Jordan/FinCloud: schedule a 30-min pricing & SOW sync next week to agree pilot scope (we recommend 6 weeks, measure hit-rate + latency + cost).
3) Ben/Eng: prepare a short prefetch/prefix residency tech note describing expected warm-up profile and any engineering constraints for the pilot.

Thanks — I’ll prepare a one-sheet and a draft SOW for Marissa to review.

— Jordan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <treynolds@fincloud.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@fincloud.com>
Date: 2026-05-07T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Warm-residency econ breakdown + pilot plan

Thanks for the clarity, Tom. I attached a two-tab spreadsheet (warm-residency-scenarios-20260507.xlsx) that expands Jordan’s scenarios and includes: detailed per-million math, sensitivity to hit-rate +/-10ppt, and an example contract line-item for a 6-week pilot. 

Top-line commercial guidance: 
- For a 120M/month pilot we can get to Tom’s effective target if we (~) hit the mid (40%) cache reuse assumption AND apply a short-term commitment discount. Example commercial anchor: list-equivalent effective rate $80 / 1M (mid-hit) with an agreed measurement window and an early-exit SLA for the pilot.
- If FinCloud can commit to a dedicated pilot (reserved capacity) we can structure a steeper per-unit discount that makes the $25k/1M target reachable for measured flows — we’ll put concrete numbers in the SOW.

Action items I’m taking now: 
- I’ll upload the SOW draft (attached) and a short pricing appendix.
- Ben: can you draft the 1-pager on prefix residency warm-up characteristics by EOD Friday? I’ll include it in the pilot SOW.
- Tom/Sara: please confirm the procurement contact and any PO timeline constraints so we can align the pilot start date (we’re targeting week of 5/24 to allow 2 weeks of prep).

Procurement note: we included Procurement on this thread to speed review. If you prefer a separate channel for legal/redlines, let us know.

Attachments: warm-residency-scenarios-20260507.xlsx, redwood-pilot-sow-draft.pdf

Regards,
Marissa Cole | Head of Commercial Programs, Redwood Inference
